title: sort() compares as text by default
why_it_matters: Numbers sort in an order that looks completely wrong.
explanation: Without a compare function, sort converts items to strings and compares them letter by letter, so '10' comes before '9'. Pass (a, b) => a - b for ascending numbers, or b - a for descending.
code:
const nums = [10, 9, 1, 100];
console.log([...nums].sort());                // [1, 10, 100, 9]
console.log([...nums].sort((a, b) => a - b)); // [1, 9, 10, 100]
console.log([...nums].sort((a, b) => b - a)); // [100, 10, 9, 1]
try_it: Quiz: where does 100 land in the default sort of [5, 100, 25]? Check it.
